gen-dafont-visitor-gf-gafata: Gafata stacks its lowercase in a deep band under short stalks, with wide-eyed e shapes, while Visitor looks bent from a single length of wire. One is all pixel-era wire, the other all quiet sans-serif contemporary polish.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-geist: Nostalgic and digital, Visitor gapes its e mouths over short ascenders. Geist holds a level beat beneath it, words reading as solid blocks, and that steady plain sans footing is the strongest thing about the pairing.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-golos-text: Chunky, retro, a bit soldered together: Visitor's pulled strokes meet Golos Text, whose x-height fills the line and whose s parts widely. It reads smoothly and approachably, one stroke width carrying you down the page without a snag.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-hedvig-letters-san: Tubular wire letters up top, then Hedvig Letters Sans below. Its small letters nearly reach capital height and the c leaves a clear gap, so a long passage feels friendly and unhurried.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-heebo: Heebo holds its text in a deep central band, with curves that stop short instead of closing in, under Visitor's fixed-pressure stylus strokes. Heebo likes a size generous enough to show those open curves, so nudge it up a notch.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-hind-guntur: Visitor brings gaping e mouths and short ascenders over big bowls, like solder pulled through a nozzle. And Hind Guntur, with its steel-cable lines and wide gaps at the curve ends, can sit at a modest size without crowding.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-hind-siliguri: Approachable Hind Siliguri hums along in a flat gray line, its rounds gapped like a cracked bangle. But Visitor's nostalgic, digital heading gives that sans-serif text something to push against, and the little bump up to capitals feels gentle by comparison.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-huninn: Gaping e mouths and big bowls give Visitor its retro look. Huninn follows in modern sans-serif, its s terminals clear of the body and lowercase rising close to cap height, so the heading's quirks feel deliberate against it.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-karla: Karla opens its c wide and stands stocky, its middle band so deep the line looks sturdy. Karla's sturdiness against Visitor's tube-like thickness, holding through every bend, is the strongest thing the two share.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-khula: Khula reads modern and broad-bellied, curves holding their mouths open like a squat brush-pen stroke. Khula keeps a long passage moving smoothly, while Visitor's rope-like stems and tails stay in the heading where they belong.
